description: Controlled vocabulary defining contextual dimensions used by A.R.I.A. to determine applicability, similarity, historical relevance, and diagnostic specificity across microwave backhaul cases.

context_types.name: USER
context_types.description: The individual interacting with ARIA or materially participating in the case.

context_types.name: TECHNICIAN
context_types.description: The individual performing or reporting technical field activity.

context_types.name: ENGINEER
context_types.description: The individual responsible for or contributing engineering information, design, interpretation, or technical direction.

context_types.name: CUSTOMER
context_types.description: The customer organization associated with the case, project, standard, design, or scope.

context_types.name: CONTRACTOR
context_types.description: The contractor or subcontractor organization performing relevant work.

context_types.name: MANUFACTURER
context_types.description: The equipment manufacturer relevant to the case.

context_types.name: PRODUCT_FAMILY
context_types.description: Broad manufacturer product family relevant to the case.

context_types.name: PRODUCT
context_types.description: Specific product type or platform relevant to the case.

context_types.name: PRODUCT_VARIANT
context_types.description: A technically meaningful product variant, model, option, or sub-type.

context_types.name: HARDWARE_REVISION
context_types.description: Hardware revision or generation when differences may affect applicability or diagnosis.

context_types.name: COMPONENT
context_types.description: Specific component participating in the applicable equipment or RF architecture.

context_types.name: FIRMWARE_VERSION
context_types.description: Installed equipment firmware or software version relevant to technical behavior.

context_types.name: SOFTWARE_RELEASE
context_types.description: Applicable management-system, controller, or platform software release.

context_types.name: FREQUENCY_BAND
context_types.description: Microwave frequency band applicable to the case.

context_types.name: CHANNEL_FREQUENCY
context_types.description: Specific transmit or receive channel frequency relevant to the case.

context_types.name: CHANNEL_BANDWIDTH
context_types.description: Configured or engineered RF channel bandwidth.

context_types.name: POLARIZATION
context_types.description: Applicable RF polarization or polarization arrangement.

context_types.name: MODULATION_PROFILE
context_types.description: Applicable fixed or adaptive modulation configuration.

context_types.name: RADIO_TOPOLOGY
context_types.description: Logical and physical microwave radio architecture.

context_types.name: DIVERSITY_MODE
context_types.description: Applicable diversity architecture or mode.

context_types.name: PROTECTION_MODE
context_types.description: Applicable radio protection arrangement.

context_types.name: XPIC_STATE
context_types.description: Whether XPIC is applicable and its relevant configured or operational state.

context_types.name: MAIN_DIVERSITY_ROLE
context_types.description: Whether an observation, component, radio, or path applies to Main, Diversity, or another defined RF role.

context_types.name: PATH
context_types.description: The specific point-to-point microwave path associated with the case.

context_types.name: PATH_DISTANCE
context_types.description: Engineered or actual distance between microwave endpoints.

context_types.name: SITE
context_types.description: Specific telecommunications site associated with the case.

context_types.name: ENDPOINT
context_types.description: Specific endpoint or side of a microwave path.

context_types.name: ANTENNA_HEIGHT
context_types.description: Installed or designed antenna centerline height relevant to the case.

context_types.name: ANTENNA_MODEL
context_types.description: Specific antenna model or technically meaningful antenna type.

context_types.name: ANTENNA_DIAMETER
context_types.description: Applicable microwave antenna diameter.

context_types.name: SCOPE_OF_WORK
context_types.description: Technical work scope associated with the case.

context_types.name: PROJECT_PHASE
context_types.description: Lifecycle phase during which the condition occurred.

context_types.name: WORK_ACTIVITY
context_types.description: Specific activity being performed when the condition was observed.

context_types.name: RECENT_CHANGE
context_types.description: A recent modification, replacement, configuration change, installation activity, or other event potentially relevant to the current condition.

context_types.name: WEATHER_CONDITION
context_types.description: Relevant weather condition at or near the microwave path.

context_types.name: PRECIPITATION
context_types.description: Relevant precipitation condition or rate.

context_types.name: WIND_CONDITION
context_types.description: Relevant wind speed, gust, or direction condition.

context_types.name: TEMPERATURE_CONDITION
context_types.description: Relevant ambient or equipment temperature condition.

context_types.name: TERRAIN_TYPE
context_types.description: Terrain characteristics potentially relevant to propagation, access, or installation.

context_types.name: PATH_ENVIRONMENT
context_types.description: Environmental characteristics of the propagation path.

context_types.name: SYMPTOM_PATTERN
context_types.description: Combination and relationship of symptoms present in a case.

context_types.name: FAILURE_MODE
context_types.description: Confirmed or candidate canonical failure mode relevant to contextual comparison.

context_types.name: CASE_STAGE
context_types.description: Current diagnostic lifecycle stage.

context_types.name: PRIOR_ACTION_PATTERN
context_types.description: Relevant sequence or combination of diagnostic actions already performed.

context_types.name: PRIOR_OUTCOME_PATTERN
context_types.description: Relevant sequence or combination of outcomes already observed.

context_types.name: TIME_SINCE_INSTALLATION
context_types.description: Elapsed time between installation or commissioning and the current condition.

context_types.name: TIME_SINCE_CHANGE
context_types.description: Elapsed time between a relevant change and symptom onset.

context_types.name: FAILURE_DURATION
context_types.description: Elapsed duration of the observed abnormal condition.

context_types.name: RECURRENCE_INTERVAL
context_types.description: Elapsed time between prior resolution and recurrence of a materially related condition.

importance_classes.CRITICAL: A mismatch may substantially alter technical applicability or diagnostic probability.
importance_classes.HIGH: A match or mismatch is normally important to diagnostic similarity.
importance_classes.MODERATE: Context may improve relevance but is not normally decisive alone.
importance_classes.DYNAMIC: Importance depends on the hypothesis, symptom, product, action, or technical question being evaluated.

semantic_rules.rule: Context determines applicability and relevance but shall not independently establish causation.
ARIA shall not treat all historical cases as equally relevant. Historical evidence shall be weighted according to similarity to the current case.
Context similarity shall be multidimensional. No single context field shall automatically determine overall case similarity unless technical rules establish that field as decisive.
Context importance may change according to the hypothesis being evaluated. Firmware may be highly important to a software defect and nearly irrelevant to a visibly damaged waveguide.
A manufacturer match shall not substitute for a product match when product-specific technical differences materially affect applicability.
A product-family match shall not automatically imply that procedures, ports, configurations, alarms, or failure mechanisms are identical across products or variants.
User-specific history may modify diagnostic priors, communication strategy, expected information quality, and route selection, but shall not override validated current technical evidence.
Customer context shall influence reasoning only where customer-specific design, standards, configuration, workflow, acceptance criteria, or historical patterns are technically relevant.
Missing context shall be represented as unknown rather than assumed.
A conflict in a critical context dimension may sharply reduce the relevance of a historical case even when other dimensions match.
ARIA shall preserve hierarchical context relationships such as Manufacturer to Product Family to Product to Product Variant without requiring knowledge to be stored as a hierarchical directory.
Context entities shall be reusable graph entities rather than duplicated descriptive strings whenever a canonical entity exists.
Recent changes occurring shortly before symptom onset may receive increased diagnostic relevance but shall not automatically be assumed causal.
The same historical case may have different similarity scores when evaluated against different hypotheses.
Similarity shall support probability estimation and retrieval but shall not be treated as proof that two cases share the same root cause.
